newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures grind upward to mixed close.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures grind upward to mixed close.

text.p: Lethargic pit trading saw IMM currency futures grind upward and end at barely mixed levels.
Most units showed little change after a day of uninspired range-trade as the market eyed Tuesday's U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting.
"All the decent-size players are out of the market before FOMC tomorrow," said one floor broker near midday. "If you saw a 100-lot trade, people were talking about it."
The most-prevalent prediction was that the FOMC meeting would result in a quarter-point hike in the U.S. Federal funds rate target, which currently stands at 5.25 percent.
Turnover stayed scanty before that meeting, with exchange price boards showing volume of roughly 9,800 contracts in June marks, 9,900 Swiss francs and 8,500 yen futures.
Sterling jumped after fourth-quarter U.K. current account was in surplus versus forecasts for a deficit, and U.K.'s 1996 balance stood at a small shortfall of 14 million sterling.
Marks nudged upward briefly when Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said a U.S. hike could push German rates higher, which he said "cannot be desirable in current conditions."
June marks lacked momentum, however, despite probing above good resistance at $0.5950, or about 1.6900 spot.
